items.note: Gemeenteblad 2025, 558275 (publication date 19-12-2025; adopted by the council 16 Dec 2025). Tarieventabel 2026 ch.1: Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage, Muntgarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Ursulinengarage and Parkeerterrein Centrum-Noord: 0.17 per 6 minutes, 1.70 per hour, 6.60 day rate, 24h/7 days. Art. 11: levy starts 1 Jan 2026 (the ordinance itself is in force the day after publication). Title matches. Wording 'effective 1 January 2026' is fine for the levy. Note the 2026 rate is unchanged from 2025 (see index 2), so the draft summary must not imply a rise.

Same Gemeenteblad. Ch.2 zones 1 and 2 (2.1-2.4): 0.17/6 min, 1.70/h, 6.60/day, Mon-Sat 09.00-18.00; 'Parkeertijd maximaal 2 uur' lists (2.2/2.4) Beekstraat, Korenmarkt, Hegstraat, Emmasingel, Dries (parkeerstrook) with only hourly rate (no day rate). Art. 8: naheffingsaanslag EUR 82.00 (2025: 78.80). All as written.

Cited page (Gemeenteblad 2024, 541494; published 23-12-2024, adopted 18 Dec 2024, levy from 1 Jan 2025) confirms 1.70/h and 6.60/day for garages and zones in 2025, and (art. 11) that it replaced the 2024 ordinance adopted 20 Dec 2023. It does NOT state the 2024 hourly or day rates (1.60 / 6.40): it shows 2024 only for permits and the naheffing (76.70). The 1.60/6.40 figures ARE correct but come from a different document, Gemeenteblad 2023, 557263 (https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2023-557263.html, adopted 20 Dec 2023, which I opened: 1.60/h and 6.40/day). Caller may add that source and restore the 2024 clause; text below is limited to what the cited page supports. That 2026 keeps 1.70/6.60 is supported by gmb-2025-558275 (index 0), not by this page.
items.corrected_text: The 2025 parking tax ordinance, adopted on 18 December 2024 (published 23 December 2024, levy from 1 January 2025), set garage and street tariffs at 1.70 euros per hour and 6.60 euros per day, with an enforcement surcharge of 78.80 euros (76.70 in 2024).

items.note: 2026 table: ch.4.1 24/7 garage subscription EUR 600.00 (2025: 600.00) for Centrumgarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage, Ursulinengarage, Walburgpassage; 4.2 OV-traveller (Stationspleingarage or Centrumgarage) 504.00; 4.3 Centrum-Noord 298.50 (2025) -> 313.90 (2026). 3.1/3.2 residents zone 1 and 2: 156.95 (2025: 153.80); 3.3 zone 3 residents 40.15 (2025: 38.90). All as written. The 2025 ordinance (gmb-2024-541494) shows Centrum-Noord 298.50 for 2025 and 288.20 for 2024, so the 298.50 still shown on weert.nl/parkeerabonnement-parkeergarage-of-terrein (read today) is the 2025 price, i.e. that page is out of date; the Gemeenteblad table is the authoritative source for 313.90.
2026 table 3.8 digital visitor scheme residents zone 3: uurtarief EUR 0.15; 3.9 businesses: uurtarief EUR 0.30. As written.

Gemeenteblad 2023, 284792 published 30-06-2023; art. 11: effective date 20 June 2023 (signed Weert, 20 June 2023). Art. 3 zones 1 and 2 paid street parking; art. 4 and art. 5/8 list exactly seven garages/lots (Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage, Ursulinengarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage, Parkeerterrein Centrum-Noord) with payment afterwards, 24 hours a day Mon-Sun; art. 7 street hours Mon-Sat 09:00-18:00; art. 6 zone 3 lists 66 numbered streets including Maaseikerweg (28), Parallelweg (39), Spoorstraat (58), Suffolkweg (59). All as written. Caveat: the 2026 tariff table refers to articles 3 and 4 of the 'vigerende' designation decision for hours, whereas in this 2023 text the corresponding hours are articles 7 and 9, so a later version may be in force; the item correctly speaks of the 2023 decision only. Researcher flag confirmed: Parallelweg is a zone 3 permit street.

2023 decision art. 9: permit parking Mon-Sat 09:00-18:00 and Thursday until 20:00; streets near the hospital Mon-Sat 09:00-20:00 and Thursday until 21:00; Wilhelminasingel (Beekstraat-Molenpoort) night regime. 2026 tariff table ch.8: Mon-Sat 09.00-18.00/20.00, Thursday 09.00-21.00. The draft's hedge that exact current hours should be checked is correct and the comparison is accurate.

Cited page weert.nl/parkeermogelijkheden-en-tarieven (read 21 Oct 2026) supports: paid street parking Mon-Sat 09.00-18.00; on koopavonden (Thursday evening), (koop)zondagen and official holidays no payment on the street; disabled-badge holders park free up to 3 hours on general disabled bays on the street in the centre, not in garages; garages/barrier lots charge 24h. The claim that permit holders are exempt from the 2-hour limit and may not use garages is NOT on this page; it is on weert.nl/parkeervergunning-bewoners (true there: 'Maximaal 2 uur parkeren is niet van toepassing op vergunninghouders'; permit not valid in garages). Dropped from the corrected text because the cited URL does not carry it.
items.corrected_text: The municipal parking page (read on 21 October 2026) says paid street parking applies Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00 and that no payment is needed on the street on shopping evenings (Thursday evening), (shopping) Sundays and official public holidays. Disabled badge holders may park free for up to 3 hours, with a parking disc, on general disabled bays on the street in the centre; this does not apply in garages or other parking places. Garages and lots with a barrier charge 24 hours a day.

items.note: Page weert.nl/parkeervergunning-bewoners (and weert.nl/parkeren named in the title) confirms: max 2 permits per address in zone 1 and 2, max 3 in zone 3 (third by email), minus own parking space or driveway; listed addresses (Beekstraat, Bassin, Begijnenhofstraat etc.) get no street permit under building-permit agreements. Employees in zone 1/2 only get a zone 2 permit and residents cannot expect to park in front of their door: both on weert.nl/parkeren (FAQ), verified. NOT on either page: that those addresses 'must use a garage' (only a 2021 tender memo says so; the current pages say only that those with more vehicles can take a garage subscription). Removed.
items.corrected_text: Page read on 21 October 2026: residents in zones 1 and 2 may receive at most 2 street permits per address and in zone 3 at most 3, minus any private parking space or driveway; for some addresses in the centre no street permit is issued under agreements in the building permit. Employees working in zone 1 and 2 businesses can only get a zone 2 street permit, and the municipality says residents cannot expect to park in front of their door.

items.note: Municipal page (read 21 Oct 2026) lists six garages with Centrumgarage 'gelegen onder het stadhuis' and the lot Centrum-Noord, and says the Q-Park P+R terrein Parallelweg 'is niet in beheer van de gemeente en heeft eigen parkeertarieven'. It does not state in so many words that the municipality itself operates the six garages and Centrum-Noord (that wording appears only in a 2021 tender memo, 'in eigen beheer'). Q-Park operator of P+R Parallelweg is confirmed by both weert.nl and Q-Park's own page (index 10). Reworded to what the cited page states.
items.corrected_text: The municipal parking page (read on 21 October 2026) lists six car parks in the centre (Centrumgarage under the town hall, Walburgpassage, Ursulinengarage, Poort van Limburg, Stationspleingarage, Muntgarage) and the Centrum-Noord lot, all charged at the municipal rates. It lists the P+R lot at Parallelweg as 'Q-Park', says it is not managed by the municipality and has its own tariffs.

items.note: TenderNed publication 226166 (API record opened): 'Digitale uitgifte parkeerproducten Weert', Gemeente Weert, published 2021-04-26, EU open procedure, contract start 2021-09-01 (completion date field 2025-09-01), notice type Aankondiging van een opdracht, flagged as awarded. The attached document is 'Bijlage 15.1 - Processen verstrekken parkeerproducten Weert' (2-page memo, opened and read in full). It says bundle applications are 'handmatig aangemaakt in Parkbase van IP Parking, een koppeling met dit systeem is niet noodzakelijk' and subscriptions are 'handmatig aangemaakt in Parkbase', and that invoices must be sent 'vanuit het nieuwe systeem'. So Parkbase/IP Parking is the existing system described in the 2021 tender papers, not the winner of the tender; the memo does not say who was awarded the contract, and it is a 2021 document. The draft's present-tense 'are managed' is too strong. Researcher flag (tender naming IP Parking's Parkbase) holds only in this limited sense.
items.corrected_text: In April 2021 the municipality published a European open tender for the digital issue of parking products (permits, subscriptions, bundles), with the contract planned to start on 1 September 2021. A memo attached to the tender describing the processes at that time says that bundle applications and garage subscriptions were created manually in Parkbase, a system of IP Parking, and that a link to that system was not required. The memo does not say who won the tender, and the arrangement may have changed since 2021.

News item of 9-10-2026 and the report (07 Verslag, 3 pages, read in full): meeting Monday 5 October 2026, 33 participants (inwoners, wijkraden, ondernemers, raadsleden); presentation covers possible car-free station square, new southern entrance, tunnel for car traffic; 'De getoonde plannen zijn nog geen besluiten, maar een eerste toekomstbeeld' (both news page and report). Worded correctly as possible, not decisions. Researcher flag confirmed. Note the embankment-parking slide is part of the same non-binding picture.

corrected_summary: Weert (Limburg) charges for parking in and around its centre. Street parking in zones 1 and 2 is paid Monday to Saturday 09:00-18:00, zone 3 is a permit-only area, and six municipal garages plus the surface lot Centrum-Noord charge 24 hours a day. Under the 2026 tariff table (council decision of 16 December 2025, levy from 1 January 2026) the rate is 1.70 euros per hour and 6.60 euros per day in the garages and on the street, unchanged from the 2025 ordinance, and the enforcement surcharge is 82.00 euros. A 24/7 garage subscription costs 600 euros a year, a Centrum-Noord subscription 313.90 euros, and a resident street permit 156.95 euros in zones 1 and 2 and 40.15 euros in zone 3. The 500-hour employee parking bundle (100 euros) is temporarily unavailable for three busy garages (Centrumgarage, Walburgpassage and Poort van Limburg) because of high parking pressure. The garages list 22 electric charge points in total. The P+R lot at Parallelweg by the station is run by Q-Park, is not managed by the municipality and has its own tariffs (295 spaces according to Q-Park). The municipality announced that street card readers for the Weerterlandpas and Stadsparkeren card stop working from 1 October 2026 because 2G is being phased out. The station area is the subject of a draft Spoorzone vision: at a meeting on 5 October 2026 the municipality showed a possible car-free station square, a new southern entrance and a car tunnel, which it says are not decisions. The council papers behind the 2025 parking standards note could not be opened because the council site was offline, so their content and adoption are not confirmed, and the old Centrum-Noord price of 298.50 euros still shown on one municipal page is the 2025 price.
